articles.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 3
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks lays out the blueprint at running back for Week 3.
articles.body:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this RB column, a WR column on Thursdays and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available .

1. Jahmyr Gibbs (vs. NYJ) - 124.5 proj. total yards

The Lions' OL is beat up with their starting C on IR and their starting LG and RT missing Week 2. That's about the only negative to say here. Gibbs managed 20.3 half PPR points on exactly 20.3 expected half PPR points in Week 2. That'll do. Gibbs has a monster game incoming given the matchup. The Lions project for 27.5 points (fifth) this week. Since Week 10 of last year, the Jets have been allowing the most fantasy points per game to RBs, adjusting for schedule.

2. Kenneth Walker (at MIA) - 112.5 proj. total yards

There is nothing negative to say. Walker is the RB1 on RB1 overall usage, while breaking the most tackles. He set a career high in targets (10) last week, and the Chiefs' entire offense looks competent right now. Meanwhile, the ACC Dolphins have the youngest defense in the NFL. It's not a surprise that the Chiefs are first in projected points at 29.0.

3. Bijan Robinson (at GB) - 123.5 proj. total yards

Let's just throw out the first two games with Cooper Rush . In 12 games with Michael Penix Jr., Robinson is the RB1 overall (21.6 half PPR points) on RB2 overall usage (18.7 expected points). Even though Penix is a gunslinger type, Bijan doesn't have a drop in target share either. We should be back to normalcy. That doesn't mean the Falcons will be good on offense (29th in projected points this week), but they won't be a disgrace like they were to open the year. The Packers defense looks much improved this year with new DC Jonathan Gannon, getting breakouts from DE Lukas Van Ness and S Javon Bullard .

4. Christian McCaffrey (vs. ARI) - 98.5 proj. total yards

There shouldn't be too much panic on McCaffrey's status as a Round 1 guy. He's definitely not in the legendary-RB phase of his career, but the 49ers offense looks like '03 Barry Bonds and McCaffrey is getting the high-value touches. He scored two goal-line touchdowns and had another goal-line attempt on a separate drive. Kaelon Black wasn't on the field in any of these situations. McCaffrey also has a 23% target share (RB3) and 4.5 receptions per game (RB5).

Is it the worst thing if Black is complementing between the 20s on pure runs? Those historically give us 0.4 fantasy points per touch. We're here for the targets (~one fantasy point) and goal-line carries (~four fantasy points). CMC's the RB9 on RB9 usage so far, and it's been in the most sustainable way possible.

5. Derrick Henry (at DAL) - 106.5 proj. total yards

Henry is the RB3 on RB7 usage so far, averaging 20 carries for 106 rushing yards. Who could have seen this coming? The offense will be more potent with Zay Flowers (hamstring) likely, but not assuredly, back, and the matchup is a very good one with the Cowboys missing their top LB and a S. They also haven't gelled on tape either. The thing to watch would be LT Ronnie Stanley (toe) actually suiting up. Without him, the Ravens OL is in tough shape.

As for the four targets last week, I'd largely ignore that as a trend. There was a screen for Henry early on, but the other targets were of the check-down variety. He still only ran a route on 14-of-40 dropbacks. It's the same role. That is totally, totally fine.

6. James Cook III (vs. LAC) - 97.5 proj. total yards

Cook may not lead the NFL in carries and rushing yards per game like he did last year because the Bills are now slightly more pass-heavy (51% neutral pass), but it's really not going to matter all that much. The Bills are second in projected points (28.75) against a meme-worthy Chargers team that is struggling defensively with a new, inexperienced DC. The real thing to take away from early results is that the suggestion of Cook being more involved as a receiver is likely fake news. He has the same targets per route as usual.

7. Jonathan Taylor (vs. HOU) - 97.5 proj. total yards

The Colts will miss Alec Pierce (heel/ankle), as he's the one who actually opens up lanes over the middle of the field, but I have a lot of faith in HC Shane Steichen's offensive plan. Taylor has been elite with Daniel Jones , and that has carried over into 2026 (RB4 on RB4 usage) despite the Colts being ninth in scoring. Jones isn't 100% but he's good enough at 85% to keep this offense afloat.

Indianapolis projects for 19.75 points (25th) because of the matchup with the Texans. Houston only allowed 17.0 half-PPR points to opposing RB rooms last year (27th) and allowed just 93 YPG (31st). Taylor had 21-86-0 rushing with 3-36-0 receiving in Week 13 against Houston with a limping DJ at QB. He was also shut down with a backup QB in Week 18, but we should throw that game out.

8. Ashton Jeanty (at NO) - 90.5 proj. total yards

Jeanty was not nearly as effective against the Chargers as he was against the ACC Dolphins. Jeanty was stuffed on four straight carries inside the five-yard line in the first quarter, then had three drops as a receiver throughout the game. Over two weeks, his 0.11 missed tackles per carry and 0.4 yards before contact are amongst the worst in the league. The good news is the workload is actually just elite. He's the RB3 in usage (23.6 expected half PPR points) while playing 75% of the snaps. Unfortunately, late in the game, Jeanty's right ankle was being looked at by trainers on the sideline, the same one that was rolled up on in training camp.

The matchup is a neutral one. The Raiders project for 20.75 points (21st), and the Saints defense has been alright against two great offenses (Lions and Ravens) with EDGE Chase Young playing great ball. The Saints were 20th against fantasy RBs last year, then Gibbs and Henry averaged 4.9 YPC in Weeks 1-2.

9. Chase Brown (at PIT) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Brown is an excellent buy low. He's the RB5 in expected half PPR points (17.8) on RB8 carries (18.0 per game) and RB8 receptions (4.0 per game). He's somehow just the RB19 in actual points after a very difficult matchup last week. The Bengals are running the ball under center with Brown, which likely will create more explosive opportunities throughout the season.

The matchup isn't great again, though. The Bengals project for 23.0 points (12th), and the Steelers have been the third-best fantasy defense since Week 11 last year, adjusting for schedule. They have a great DL. That said, Brown did catch them for a huge game (18.7 PPR) in Week 11 last year with Joe Flacco and then scored 19.0 PPR points in his last game against the Steelers with Joe Burrow available.

10. Breece Hall (at DET) - 82.5 proj. total yards

Hall has lost a couple of inside-the-10-yard-line TDs to Braelon Allen , but Hall will get some of those eventually and is getting a ton otherwise. He's the RB11 on RB13 usage, averaging 19.0 carries and 3.5 receptions per game. That's great stuff when Hall also looks healthy on tape. He had a real highlight play in the screen game last week, for example.

The Lions matchup is an underrated good one. I'm expecting negative game script, as the Jets defense isn't ready for them, but Hall can catch five+ passes in those scripts, just like he had last week. The Lions also just gave up 203 rushing yards last week to the Bills. It's so refreshing to see the Jets project for 20.5 points on the road against a Super Bowl-caliber team. They are officially competent right now — that's never been true for the entirety of Hall's career.

11. Omarion Hampton (at BUF) - 75.5 proj. total yards

Hampton is a tough tackle when running up the middle and has the speed for explosives when given open space. The Chargers are loading him up with 17.5 carries per game (RB9) to start the season, too, but unfortunately, those are the lone positives.

Hampton's two fumbles are inexcusable, and his cutback vision and lateral ability have been clear weaknesses in this outside zone and perimeter-based system. There will be times when he'll turn the corner, but the De'Von Achane types are just so much better at adjusting their point of attack. Hampton is also far less involved as a receiver (0 and 2 receptions, respectively) than the other OC Mike McDaniel backs. I'm not sure the blocking up front will get better either. The interior OL is not changing, and the TE room is significantly worse at blocking moving forward with David Njoku and Charlie Kolar hitting IR. Hampton can't totally bust, but he does have "silent killer" vibes (RB20 on RB21 usage), as the Chargers' schedule significantly tightens up for the next two months.

12. De'Von Achane (vs. KC) - 90.5 proj. total yards

The Dolphins will be a pretty rough watch all year. They're too young, too inexperienced to sustain long drives. That will prevent Achane from being a top-8 fantasy RB most likely. The good news, once again if any, is the Dolphins are absolutely feeding him the rock and they're doing it in the exact same ways the 2025 Dolphins were doing. The run game is creative and playing to his strengths, though they haven't executed the timing perfectly up front with their TEs/FBs in particular. He's handled the goal-line carry in Week 2, too. His carries per game (15.5) are up from 2024-25 (13.4).

Achane's targets per game (5.5) are basically the same as his 2024-25 stretch (5.2), too. He's the RB12 in receptions per game (3.5) right now because a few of them have gone incomplete, but the Dolphins and Malik Willis aren't structurally changing his receiving role. He's getting the same number of targets as normal, with other first-read targets and garbage-time check downs sprinkled in. I don't see a reason to blame the coaching staff so far.

Long story short, Achane is the RB8 in expected half PPR points. The efficiency has been brutal, but Achane has been a model breaker for years, if you're bold enough to buy low as a fringe RB1. We can't expect him to sniff his career 5.5 YPC or 6.0 YPT, but I predict it won't stay at 3.5 and 4.5 either.

13. Chuba Hubbard (at CLE) - 80.5 proj. total yards

Look at Chuba Hubbard right now versus all other RBs who had an ADP of 60+ on Yahoo.

Jonathon Brooks (groin) had a setback in Week 2 and is officially week-to-week, but he wasn't much of a factor even before that. It'd be a very big surprise if Hubbard lost his clear-cut starting job in 2026 at this point, barring injury. He's the RB8 on RB14 usage so far, and he did something very similar in 2024, too. Hubbard played 77% of snaps in the first year with the current coaching staff, leading to an RB12 on RB7 usage on RB4 overall rush yards over expected (+24%).

He's at +14% in that same metric right now, and Hubbard is the RB1 in success rate (min. 10 RB carries per game). The Panthers have invested a lot in their OL over recent offseasons, and it's paying off now. Bryce Young is also playing poised in a more aggressive offense and suddenly has two "WR1" talents. It's an underrated environment.

14. Saquon Barkley (at CHI) - 89.5 proj. total yards

We'll learn more about his availability (stinger) later in the week. Without him, Tank Bigsby was the early-down runner while Will Shipley played a bulk of the pass downs. On tape, the Eagles' interior OL and TE blocking are well below average. Philly is 31st in RB success rate through two weeks. This is unfortunately closer to the 2025 splits than the 2024 splits. Barkley is the RB17 on RB6 usage from 2025 Week 1 to 2026 Week 1, throwing out last week's part-time outing.

The good news is the Bears defense is one to target, especially with a third-string QB starting against a Vic Fangio defense. Chicago allowed the sixth-most rush yards in 2025, then has allowed 23.7 half-PPR points to Chuba Hubbard in Week 1 and 103 rushing yards to Aaron Jones Sr. last Sunday. The Eagles project for 23.0 points (13th) as road favorites on Monday Night Football.

15. Javonte Williams (vs. BAL) - 79.5 proj. total yards

Williams is the RB11 on RB5 expected half PPR points per game since 2025. He's the RB14 on RB10 usage this year in the same exact role with absolutely nobody behind him on the depth chart.

Since Week 10 of last year, the Ravens have allowed 66 rushing yards per game to RBs, the second fewest. This is definitely not a great matchup for Williams, yet the Cowboys project for 24.5 points (sixth) and we're here for the check-downs and goal-line carries more than anything else. He's a TD-or-bust fringe RB1/2.

16. Aaron Jones Sr. (at TB) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Jones' first game without Jordan Mason (IR, finger) was a success. He scored 10.5 half PPR points on 10.5 expected half PPR points (RB27), despite going catchless in positive game script in rainy conditions. Jones played 90% of the snaps heading into halftime and would've hovered in that range if not for a momentary knee scare. He's good (for now). Jones hasn't looked "washed" on tape early in the year, and he's more likely to hit explosives with Kyler Murray standing next to him. He's also far more likely to catch passes when it's not rainy with a lead. In general, bellcow backs like this are must-starts in fantasy. Keep in mind that he's the RB20 on RB13 usage without Mason available since 2024.

Since Week 10 of last year, the Buccaneers have allowed the most receiving yards per game to RBs (48) and their off-ball LB tape has been brutal this season in particular. There will be issues running the ball up the gut against DT Vita Vea , but the Bucs aren't as scary as they've been over the past five years with HC Todd Bowles. The Vikings are projected for 22.0 points (16th) on the road.

17. Kyren Williams (at DEN) - 71.5 proj. total yards

Williams is the RB9 on RB14 usage since Week 10 of last year when Blake Corum was mixing in for about 33% of the snaps. The thing to remember is the Rams averaged 30.4 points per game during that stretch, so they have to be elite, elite for Williams to be a top-10 RB. It's a drive-for-drive rotation in 2026, with Williams more likely to play in chase mode and more likely to get designed receptions.

The Rams project for 24.0 points in Denver this week, so a tier below the split from the paragraph above. The Broncos lost DT John Franklin-Myers this offseason and were absolutely lit up by Kenneth Walker in Week 1 before looking a bit better against the Jaguars' RBs last week. Since 2025, Denver is second-best against fantasy RBs, allowing just 99 rushing YPG to RBs, so I think the Walker game will end up being the outlier. This is a difficult matchup.

18. David Montgomery (at IND) - 59.5 proj. total yards

The Texans are rotating their RBs by drive. David Montgomery starts, but Woody Marks will play many snaps in a row. They view this tandem as capable in all situations, rather than rotating them by situation. If Marks' drive ends near the end zone, I'm not sold that Montgomery gets the goal-line carry. Last week, Montgomery had one carry in the second half while in negative script, too.

Beyond that, the reality is the Texans' ground game is broken. Both RBs are bottom-three in yards per carry among RBs with 10+ carries per game. It's not even their fault either. The OL is just not talented enough, and the QB being a statue doesn't help the numbers either. I don't know how this changes.

The good news, and it's very good news, is the Colts defense is equally broken. Their LBs can't play, and their DBs aren't making plays. Kenneth Walker and Derrick Henry had great games against them in traditional, downhill roles. The Texans being projected for 22.5 points (15th) is not a surprise. Montgomery is a low-end, TD-or-bust RB2.

19. Jaylen Warren (vs. CIN) - 78.5 proj. total yards

Warren has outplayed Rico Dowdle in each phase to start the year. The pass protection difference is night and day, with Dowdle making critical errors multiple times in each game. Warren is also the better receiver in general. And the eye test and numbers suggest Warren has been more effective on the ground, too. Warren's -1% rush yards over expected are much better than Dowdle's -47%.

More importantly to that is the Dowdle toe injury. He left the game, returned and then was ruled out. Without Dowdle on the field, Warren played 50-of-52 snaps, only losing two to special-teamer Travis Homer . The Steelers offense is beyond disorganized right now, but there is potential for real bellcow usage if Dowdle misses. With Dowdle, Warren is the RB31 on RB20 usage. Dowdle was still in a walking boot on Wednesday. This assumes he is out.

20. Cam Skattebo (vs. TEN) - 73.5 proj. total yards

Skattebo is the clear lead back, but there are three backs involved. In Week 2, Najee Harris subbed in for a goal-line carry that was stuffed by DT Aaron Donald , while Devin Singletary mixes in as a change-of-pace. Harris has very clear atrophy on his left leg, stemming from his torn Achilles; when push comes to shove, I think it'll be a lot of Skattebo.

Skattebo did have four receptions last week in negative game script, after scaring us with 0 grabs in the opener. This isn't as clean of a role as it was during his rookie season, but he's managing low-end RB2 numbers. Skattebo is the RB23 on RB19 usage and plays a big part in being the heartbeat, energy-wise.

21. Bucky Irving (vs. MIN) - 77.5 proj. total yards

Since 2024, the Vikings are sixth-best against fantasy RBs. They've only allowed five RBs to reach 20+ half PPR points; two of those were Jahmyr Gibbs. Their swarm style prevents RBs from getting into the route, and it could incentivize more snaps out of Kenneth Gainwell this time around. Minnesota has also added EDGE Dallas Turner and DT Jalen Redmond, full breakouts to the equation this season. Over the last four games dating back to last year, Minnesota is the very best fantasy RB defense, allowing just 11.4 half PPR points to the entire room.

22. Bhayshul Tuten (vs. NE) - 66.5 proj. total yards

The Jaguars are using a rotation at RB, but Tuten is by far the most involved. He's the RB22 on RB28 usage through two weeks with difficult rushing matchups to start. They aren't throwing the ball to RBs, and I totally get that with their WR/TE depth, but Tuten is getting some of the goal-line work. He had a Wildcat carry for a TD at the one-yard line last week after being on the field the play prior to bring them down to the goal line. Chris Rodriguez Jr. had a third-and-1 Wildcat carry earlier in the game, however. I'd guess they split goal-line work this year. Between the 20s, it's been a ton of Tuten and he's breaking tackles at a high clip. It's not a big win so far, but Tuten is holding the Round 5 line.

The matchup is another difficult one. The Patriots have great DTs and a scheme that will put more players into the box than most. New England was the best fantasy RB defense of 2025. Jacksonville's 24.25 points this week are more likely to come through the air.

23. Jeremiyah Love (at SF) - 59.5 proj. total yards

Love remains in a clear 1-2 punch committee. He had 13.2 expected half PPR points in Week 1's upset win and 8.2 expected points in last week's predictable blowout loss against one of the best rushing defenses of the decade. Arizona had no chance in either phase, and if this happens more often, the Cardinals will have no choice but to get Love more involved. He's just operating at another speed than Tyler Allgeier, who had the lone goal-line attempt this season.

Love hasn't been a designed target player in the regular season so far, which is the easiest way to get him going some. All three of his receptions last game were more of the check-down variety. He has an 11% target share this year, yet none of them have been screens. It's not the best role until proven otherwise, and everything out of the staff's mouth suggests it'll be a little bit before we see Love unleashed.

I could see a divisional game after being shut down on offense the previous week being the time to unleash Love. The 49ers' game is a big one for the Cardinals, and they are down DTs and depth EDGEs right now. Love catching 4-6 passes in negative game script would not be a surprise to me. He'll always be up against a lowly 19.5-point team total, but I could see a career-high in touches here.

24. Quinshon Judkins (vs. CAR) - 57.5 proj. total yards

Swift can't be viewed as the RB1 he's scored like to open the year without Caleb Williams (hamstring) and Tyson Bagent (concussion). The Bears only project for 18.5 points (29th) against an Eagles defense that has been very good since DC Vic Fangio showed up. The Bears will continue rotating drives between Swift and Kyle Monangai, and now it's for an offense that we don't love. Here is how many half PPR points Swift has scored when the Bears finished with 21 points or fewer since 2025: 9.0, 5.3, 9.7, 14.1, 14.4, and 12.4. That's an average of 10.8, equivalent to the RB23 on a per-game basis.

Etienne has been the biggest non-injury bust based on his role through two weeks. He lost early-down work to Kendre Miller in Week 1, before Miller was healthy-scratched last week in favor of Alvin Kamara. The role stayed the same. Etienne is splitting early-down work and is rarely playing late downs because UDFA rookie FB C.J. Donaldson is more trusted in protection. That reeks. Etienne only had 5.8 expected half PPR points (RB42) last week and would not have a FLEX-worthy profile if not for the garbage-time receptions versus the Lions in the opener. The Saints also used Tyler Shough in Tush Push situations (with Etienne on the field), so the needle we're threading for Etienne right now is very, very narrow. It didn't help that Etienne dropped one of his pitch attempts and then bobbled the next one after the timing between the motion player and Shough's pitch was off.

Oh yeah, I almost forgot — emerging star LT Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) is out for months now.

27. Tony Pollard (at NYG) - 53.5 proj. total yards

Through two weeks, Price is the RB31 on RB27 usage, which is very similar to the Kenneth Walker split in the regular season when Zach Charbonnet was stealing the high-value opportunities.

Last week, Price started each half and ended with 11.7 expected half PPR points. He fumbled in a big pile in the second quarter but wasn't directly benched. Emanuel Wilson played in each half and handled most of the short-yardage and goal-line work, while George Holani played the obvious pass-down snaps. Price picked up a chest injury in the second half, so it was largely Wilson in "run out the clock" mode. At the very end of the game, TE A.J. Barner scored on a Tush Push, too.

29. TreVeyon Henderson (at JAX) - 53.5 proj. total yards

Week 2 was a major win for Henderson. Rhamondre Stevenson started the game, but he fumbled the ball in a nonsense yards-after-the-catch moment shortly after. The Patriots rode Henderson for a larger-than-normal split afterwards. He started the second half and ended with 16 carries to Stevenson's 6.

Henderson split between new LG Alijah Vera-Tucker and switched-position C Jared Wilson for a nearly untouched rushing TD, but the rest of the game was forgettable. He wasn't targeted nor tasked with a single pass-protection rep, and the Patriots had zero plays within the five-yard line. We head into Week 3 without major answers of what the split will be. I'd lean Henderson as the touch leader with Stevenson still the favorite for goal-line reps. It's worth noting that the Patriots have only averaged 16.7 expected half PPR points to their RB room through two weeks (27th).

Since Week 10 of last year, the Jaguars have allowed 60 yards per game to RBs, easily the best mark in the NFL.

30. Rhamondre Stevenson (at JAX) - 56.5 proj. total yards

Dobbins started in Week 2 and had quality decisions on his cutbacks on tape. Unfortunately, the blocking was poor on back-to-back goal-line carries and a botched snap and pitch from Bo Nix derailed the third attempt for a score. There were some near big plays on the ground elsewhere, but the OL just couldn't seal things off completely. I don't see a decline in his play individually, even if the results aren't kind.

The bad news is we have a soft-tissue injury to monitor now. Jonah Coleman stepped up without him late in Week 2, while RJ Harvey (hamstring) was out. The rookie went untouched on his goal-line carry for a TD and handled himself well afterwards, sliding in bounds to ice the game. But he's dealing with an injury too.

Dobbins hasn't reached 15+ half PPR points or 15+ expected half PPR points in 10-straight games as a starter in this committee approach.

32. Woody Marks (at IND) - 43.5 proj. total yards

33. Blake Corum (at DEN) - 52.5 proj. total yards

34. Kaleb Johnson (vs. ATL) - 40.5 proj. total yards

36. Tyler Allgeier (at SF) - 44.5 proj. total yards

40. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (vs. SEA) - 41.5 proj. total yards

Croskey-Merritt is the early-down starter, but he's being squeezed in multiple ways and his tape has been mixed. There was a pitch where he and Jayden Daniels weren't on the same page, leading to a fumble. Daniels also yelled at him in the 2-minute drill for not leaking out as a receiver. Bill was also late on a blitzer that forced Daniels to scramble. It wasn't mistake-free play in Week 2. White did get a carry from the five-yard line heading into halftime, which really can't happen for Bill's fantasy value. In both Week 1 and Week 2, Kaytron Allen had mop-up duties late in the game, too.

It's a bad situation with LT Laremy Tunsil out, RT Josh Conerly banged up and Jayden Daniels out weeks and weeks, most likely. Bill is the RB23 on RB32 usage through two weeks, and that feels like the best-case scenario moving forward. He's an RB3 who hopefully is on your bench.

42. Rachaad White (vs. SEA) - 39.5 proj. total yards

43. Chris Rodriguez Jr. (vs. NE) - 24.5 proj. total yards

44. Emmett Johnson (at MIA) - 40.5 proj. total yards

47. MarShawn Lloyd (vs. ATL) - 36.5 proj. total yards

Lloyd has not passed the eye test, is not trusted in pass protection and then fumbled the ball in the fourth quarter of last week. Afterwards, he played 1-of-22 snaps, with Chris Brooks playing almost all snaps until Kaleb Johnson had a couple of runs in OT. If I had to guess, it'll be Johnson with the most carries in Week 3. Even then, who cares? This Packers OL is a total disaster and now won't have RT Zach Bako-Bewele for the season. Lloyd can be dropped in shallow leagues.

48. Mike Washington Jr. (at NO) - 16.5 proj. total yards

51. Chris Brooks (vs. ATL) - 27.5 proj. total yards

53. Tyjae Spears (at NYG) - 41.5 proj. total yards

articles.title: 'Today, a Khan and a Singh won a medal for India': Satnam Singh on Asian Games rowing bronze
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Satnam Singh and Salman Khan won India's first-ever Asian Games medal in men's double sculls on Thursday, with the Indian pair claiming bronze
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Satnam Singh and Salman Khan won India's first-ever Asian Games medal in men's double sculls on Thursday, with the Indian pair claiming bronze at the Nagaragawa International Regatta Course.But for Satnam, the medal meant much more than a place on the podium."Today, a Khan and a Singh won a medal for India. I want people to remember that. Long after we are gone, this fact will live on. Salman is like a brother to me. There are things we hear and read about, and that disturbs us. I want our people to stop fighting on religious lines," Satnam told HT.The pair clocked 6:13.25 to finish third. China's Yi Xudi and Nie Yide won gold in 6:09.77, while Uzbekistan's Mekhrojbek Mamatkulov and Pavel Sorin took silver in 6:10.49. Satnam and Salman were second at the 1,500m mark but slipped to third in the final 500m.A medal that brought two journeys togetherSatnam and Salman had originally been selected for the quadruple sculls team along with Jakar Khan and Balraj Panwar. However, after a change in the team combinations, the duo was moved to the double sculls event in place of Navdeep Singh and Kulwinder Singh.Satnam admitted the change did affect them, but the two decided to focus on giving their best."I won't say we were not affected by it, but we decided to give our best. It helped that me and Salman have been training together for seven months for quadruple sculls, so we had good understanding," Satnam said.He also felt the conditions helped them."The tailwind helped us today and the waters were still. We were the lightest finalists, which helped us go faster. Both of us weigh about 85kgs each while the rest of the rowers were in 90-95kg range."Satnam's road to the podiumFor Satnam, the bronze also helped erase the disappointment of the previous Asian Games. China and Uzbekistan had won gold and silver in the event at the previous edition, although with different rowers. Satnam, who had competed with Parminder Singh, had finished last among six pairs in Hangzhou."The failure in Hangzhou had haunted me all these years and I was waiting for this Asiad to redeem myself. I was also part of the quadruple team that won a bronze there. We were on course for a silver in 2023 but I was exhausted and passed out which had cost us a second-place result. So all that weighed heavy on me coming into the competition," Satnam said.The 26-year-old comes from Fatta Maluka village in Punjab's Mansa district and is employed in the Indian Navy as a Chief Petty Officer. A former national-level handball player, Satnam also played volleyball before taking up rowing. He was inspired by London Olympian Swarn Singh Virk, who also comes from Mansa."I was into multiple sports at school, and once my PT teacher invited Swarn Singh to our school to have a word with kids. Swarn comes from Mansa as well, so he was an instant inspiration," Satnam recalled.Swarn encouraged him to take up rowing, and Satnam joined the Punjab Institute of Sports in Ropar, where he began training under Virjender Singh Cheema.Satnam joined the Navy in 2019 through the sports quota and later trained at SAI centres in Odisha and Alleppey.A promise to his motherSatnam grew up in a family with limited means. His father, Amrik Singh, grew cotton on their farm, while his mother Harjeet Kaur tailored clothes to support the family. His brother Gurpiar Singh, a soldier with the 28 Punjab Regiment based in Jammu, supported his early training. Satnam later joined the Army Rowing Node in Pune in 2022."I am happy to have given them something to cheer about after all these years. I had promised my mom that I'll make up for that Hangzhou heartbreak. I am happy to have done that," he said.Satnam is also proud of his roots and the athletes who have come from Mansa."There is something about Mansa that it produces strong people. Swarn Singh and double Asiad medallist rower Sukhmeet Singh are also from here. A lot of our boys join the army," he said.Late Punjabi singer Siddhu Moosewala was another of Satnam's heroes."He remains an absolute star. I listen to his songs while warming-up," he said.From driving an Uber to an Asian Games medalSalman's journey to the Asian Games podium has also been shaped by struggle. Born in Pure Dhingai in Uttar Pradesh's Amethi, Salman is the eldest of four brothers and two sisters. His father, Mohd Kasim Khan, worked in a truck-body construction company in Tauru, Haryana, where Salman completed his schooling. His life changed when his father died of dengue when Salman was 18. He then drove an Uber in Delhi to support his family before joining the Bombay Engineering Group of the Indian Army in 2018.It was there that Salman discovered rowing. His 6'4" frame and raw power caught the attention of coaches, and he began training at the Army Rowing Node under senior coach Kudrat Ali and Training Officer Major Nagendra Hooda."It feels like a dream come true. I was expecting to win a medal at the Asian Games, and I am delighted that I could fulfil that expectation. But this is only the beginning; my next target is the Los Angeles Olympics," Salman, a Naib Subedar in the Army, said."I know what struggle means in life, but I never lost hope. I kept working hard and continued to believe in myself."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vithya Ramaraj turns on the afterburners, holds off Vietnam by 0.08 seconds as India storm to mixed 4x400m silver at Asian Games
articles.summary: India added another athletics medal to its Asian Games tally on Thursday as the mixed 4x400m relay team of Manu, Vithya Ramaraj, Poovamma and Vishal TK
articles.body: India added another athletics medal to its Asian Games tally on Thursday as the mixed 4x400m relay team of Manu, Vithya Ramaraj, Poovamma and Vishal TK won silver in Nagoya.Vishal TK started for India but could not make much ground early on. Poovamma then took over and India risked slipping out of the medal race before a burst in the final 50m brought the team back into contention. She handed the baton to Manu with India in third.Manu kept India in the race before handing over to Vithya Ramaraj for the final leg. Vithya, known for her strong anchor legs, made up ground on the final lap and pulled India into second place to seal the silver.Asian Games full coverage | Schedule | Medal tallyBahrain's Salwa Eid Nasser had already moved clear at the front and powered her team to gold in a Games-record 3:12.87. India finished in 3:14.46, while Vietnam took bronze in 3:14.54.Earlier in the day, India's 16-year wait for a women's 10,000m medal at the Asian Games ended as Seema Kumari won bronze in Nagoya.In a race that built slowly before coming alive in the closing stages, Seema stayed in medal contention until the end. Winfred Yavi and Japan's Nozomi Tanaka broke away for a sprint finish for gold and silver, while Seema pulled clear of the rest of the field to secure third place.Yavi won gold in 32:39.18, with Tanaka taking silver in 32:41.54. Seema completed the race in 32:50.05 to win bronze.It was India's first women's 10,000m medal at the Asian Games in 16 years.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Day 5: Seema, mixed relay win athletics medals; Roshibina bags Wushu silver
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India made a strong start to its athletics campaign at the Asian Games 2026 on Thursday, winning two medals.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India made a strong start to its athletics campaign at the Asian Games 2026 on Thursday, winning two medals. The mixed 4x400m relay team won silver, while Seema won bronze in the women's 10,000m. Seema's medal was India's first athletics medal at these Games.The relay team of TS Manu, MR Poovamma, Vishal TK and Vithya Ramraj clocked 3:14.46 to finish second behind Bahrain. Bahrain won gold in a Games record time of 3:12.87.Seema ends India's wait in women's 10,000mSeema, 25, won the bronze medal in the women's 10,000m with a time of 32:50.05. Bahrain's Winfred Yavi won gold in 32:39.18, while Japan's Nozomi Tanaka took silver in 32:41.54.Seema's bronze was India's first women's 10,000m medal at the Asian Games since 2010.At the 2010 Asian Games, Preeja Sreedharan won gold and Kavita Raut claimed silver in the event.Mixed relay team adds another medalThe mixed 4x400m relay team also continued India's medal run in the event.India won gold when the event was introduced at the 2018 Asian Games and took silver at the previous edition. Thursday's result gave India its third consecutive medal in the event.The result was kept unofficial for some time after the UAE lodged a protest. The UAE was later disqualified, making India's silver medal official.India had earlier qualified for the final after finishing second in Heat 2.Roshibina wins second straight Asian Games silverIndia's Roshibina Devi Naorem won her second consecutive Asian Games silver in wushu. She lost 0-2 to China's Zhang Xiaoyu in the women's 60kg sanda final. Zhang won both rounds 5-0 to take the bout 10-0 on aggregate.Roshibina had also won silver at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games and bronze at the 2018 Jakarta-Palembang Games. She became India's most successful wushu player at the Asian Games with three medals.Roshibina had missed out on selection initially after losing the trials. She got a place in the team after original choice Divyanshi Choudhary was ruled out due to injury.Anantjeet-Parinaaz clinch historic skeet mixed-team bronzeAnantjeet Singh Naruka and Parinaaz Dhaliwal gave Indian skeet another reason to celebrate on Thursday, shooting their way to a historic bronze in the mixed team event. It was India's first-ever Asian Games medal in mixed team skeet.The bronze completed a remarkable three-medal haul for Indian skeet in just two days. Anantjeet, Bhavtegh Singh Gill and Mairaj Ahmed Khan had won the men's team bronze on Wednesday, before Parinaaz, Raiza Dhillon and Maheshwari Chauhan added another bronze in the women's team event later that day.Twenty-four hours later, Anantjeet and Parinaaz were back at the range, this time combining to ensure that India won medals in all three skeet events at the Asian Games.Rowers finally have a medal to showIndia's rowers also finished the day with a bronze medal. Satnam Singh and Salman Khan won bronze in the men's double sculls, India's first medal in the event at the Asian Games.The Indian pair stayed second until the 1,500m mark before dropping to third in the final 500m. They clocked 6:13.25.China won gold, while Uzbekistan took silver.Asha Ilango misses bronze Asha Ilango narrowly missed out on a medal in the women's triple jump. She finished fourth after producing a best jump of 13.83m, the same distance as China's Yi Li.The Chinese athlete finished ahead because her second-best jump was better. Yi had a second-best effort of 13.79m, while Asha's was 13.65m.Animesh, Gurindervir reach 100m semifinalsAnimesh Kujur qualified for the men's 100m semifinals after finishing third in Heat 1 of Round 1. He clocked 10.36 seconds. Thailand's Puripol Boonson won the heat in 9.95 seconds.National record holder Gurindervir Singh also reached the semifinals after finishing second in Heat 4 with a time of 10.38 seconds. The top three from each of the six heats and the next six fastest runners advanced to the semifinals, which will be held on Friday.Kabaddi teams continue unbeaten runBoth the Indian men's and women's kabaddi teams continued their winning runs. The men's team beat Chinese Taipei 37-21, while the women's team defeated Japan 50-25 to reach the semifinals and secure at least a bronze medal.India are the defending champions in both events.Anahat, Tanvi set up all-Indian squash quarterfinalIndia had a productive day in squash, with Anahat Singh, Tanvi Khanna, Abhay Singh and Veer Chotrani reaching the singles quarterfinals. Anahat beat Singapore's Wai Iynn Au Yeong 3-0 (11-4, 11-5, 11-7) in 19 minutes.Tanvi defeated Singapore's Wai Yhann Au Yeong 3-1 (5-11, 11-4, 11-5, 13-11) in 39 minutes. The results set up an all-Indian women's singles quarterfinal between Anahat and Tanvi.In men's singles, Abhay beat Sri Lanka's Ravindu Laksiri 3-0, while Veer defeated Malaysia's Sanjay Jeeva 3-2 after a close contest. Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar also advanced to the mixed doubles quarterfinals.Dilpreet's hat-trick powers hockey winDilpreet Singh scored a hat-trick as India beat Korea 8-2 in the men's hockey competition. It was India's third straight win and kept the team at the top of Pool A. Dilpreet scored in the 10th, 26th and 32nd minutes. Abhishek scored twice, while Shilanand Lakra, Harmanpreet Singh and Rajinder Singh also found the net.India had earlier beaten Indonesia 13-1 and Sri Lanka 16-1.Boxing, gymnastics and fencing disappointParveen was the only Indian boxer to progress on Thursday after receiving a walkover into the women's 65kg quarterfinals. Sakshi Chaudhary lost 2-3 to Kazakhstan's Alua Balkibekova in the women's 51kg pre-quarterfinals, while Sumit had to withdraw during his 70kg bout because of a knee injury.In gymnastics, Pranati Nayak finished sixth in the women's vault final. She scored 12.900 on both vaults and finished with 13.100 after a 0.20 bonus.India's fencing campaign also ended after C A Bhavani Devi and Shreya Gupta were eliminated in women's individual sabre. Bhavani reached the round of 16 after beating Mongolia's Oulen Tugsjargan 15-8, but lost 5-15 to China's Rao Xueyi in the pre-quarterfinals.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Before WWE fame, Cody Rhodes’ journey saw early wrestling success, the Stardust era, a 2016 exit, career rebuilding outside WWE and a celebrated return as a global star
articles.summary: Cody Rhodes' journey through WWE, from Stardust to his triumphant return as a top star and World Champion is explored in detail. Discover the milestones, struggles, and transformations that shaped his career.
articles.body: Cody Rhodes is now firmly established as one of the top names in WWE, but his journey to the top was anything but straightforward. Before becoming a WrestleMania main-eventer and world champion, Rhodes spent nearly a decade trying to make a name for himself inside WWE while carrying the expectations that came with being the son of WWE Hall of Famer Dusty Rhodes.His first WWE run saw tag team glory, the Legacy faction, an Intercontinental Championship run and plenty of character changes. His most controversial period was with Stardust, a colorful alter ego who would eventually become synonymous with the frustrations surrounding his final years with the company. Eventually, Rhodes left WWE in 2016 and embarked on a career path that redefined his place in pro wrestling.Cody Rhodes’ journey before leaving WWE and rebuilding his careerRhodes began his WWE career in 2006 with Ohio Valley Wrestling, before coming up to the main roster in 2007. Dusty Rhodes was the son of one of the most influential figures in the history of American wrestling, and his ambitions were deeply connected to his family legacy.Rhodes had a lot of big accomplishments in his first WWE run. WWE records credit him with two Intercontinental Championship reigns and six tag-team championship reigns during his 2007-2016 tenure. He had a 236-day Intercontinental Championship run in 2011-2012, which was a big singles accomplishment before the character changes he made later in his career.The biggest change came in 2014 when Rhodes became Stardust. The character was inspired by the Goldust persona of his half-brother Dustin Rhodes, and the two brothers would go on to team in WWE’s tag-team division.Stardust was not without successes. At Night of Champions (2014), Rhodes and Goldust won the WWE Tag Team Championship. But the character became increasingly central to the direction of Rhodes' WWE career, particularly as he looked to push into the singles main-event picture.Cody Rhodes milestonePeriodSignificanceOhio Valley Wrestling2006Began his developmental pathWWE main-roster debut2,007Started his major WWE careerLegacy with Randy Orton and Ted DiBiase2008–2010Established him in a prominent factionIntercontinental Championship2011–2012Major singles championship achievementStardust character2014–2016Defined his final WWE phaseWWE departureMay 2016Began his career outside WWECody Rhodes’ WWE career before leaving in 2016On May 22, 2016, WWE announced they had granted Rhodes’ release, making his departure from the company official. The ruling snapped a streak that started almost a decade ago during his time as a developmental player and carried into his main-roster career.The circumstances of the departure were more complicated than a single character decision. In later discussions of his career, Rhodes spoke of becoming more and more distant from his goal of becoming WWE Champion. His Stardust run had become increasingly difficult to move past, and ESPN reported he spent years trying to convince WWE leadership he could become a top-level star.After WWE, Rhodes was able to work a much wider swath of the wrestling industry. He worked for independent promotions and overseas audiences, gaining experience in situations where he was not bound to the Stardust character.This period was important because Rhodes was able to establish himself as more than just a former WWE wrestler, but as a performer that could draw attention outside of the company. He built up his profile working for well-known independent promotions and competing in big wrestling events.Cody Rhodes rebuilt his wrestling career outside WWERhodes’ independent run gave him opportunities that were difficult to duplicate during his first WWE tenure. He continued to perform in different promotions and grow his international presence, including working in Japan and other major wrestling markets.One of the biggest evolutions was All In, back in 2018. The event, which saw Rhodes work with The Young Bucks and other names in wrestling, became an important milestone in independent wrestling.The success of All In helped prove there was an appetite for big wrestling events outside of WWE. It also helped power the launch of All Elite Wrestling in 2019, where Rhodes became an Executive Vise President, along with an active performer.Rhodes’ AEW run included high-profile bouts, title shots and major storylines. More importantly, it helped get the American Nightmare character established outside of WWE.Cody Rhodes returned to WWE as a top starRhodes returned to WWE in April 2022 at WrestleMania 38, six years after his last WWE match. His surprise appearance as Seth Rollins’ opponent immediately made him a drastically different character from the Stardust-era wrestler who had left the company.Rhodes got the win in the rematch against Seth Rollins after three Cross Rhodes. WWE also pointed out how Rhodes paid tribute to his late father with the Bionic Elbow during the match.Rhodes has made his intentions clear since he returned; he wants to be WWE Champion. WWE announced immediately following WrestleMania 38 that he had a stated goal of capturing the championship.Career phaseMajor development2006–2007Developmental wrestling and WWE debut2008–2010Legacy with Randy Orton and Ted DiBiase2011–2012Intercontinental Championship success2014–2016Stardust era and eventual WWE departure2016–2018Independent wrestling and international expansion2018All In helped establish his broader industry role2019–2022AEW performer and Executive Vice President2022Returned to WWE at WrestleMania 382023–2024Back-to-back Royal Rumble victoriesWrestleMania XLDefeated Roman Reigns for the Undisputed WWE ChampionshipThe journey changed the meaning of Cody RhodesRhodes' career before WWE fame became a story of several distinct phases rather than a straightforward rise through one company. His initial WWE run proved his championship credentials, but the Stardust era and 2016 departure needed a massive reset.The time away from WWE allowed Rhodes to retool his character, polish up the American Nightmare persona and get experience in independent wrestling and AEW. Those experiences formed the basis for his eventual comeback.When Rhodes returned to WWE at WrestleMania 38, he returned after six years with a significantly different resume. His later championship success was the culmination of a journey that started under the pressure of following Dusty Rhodes, continued through the limitations of Stardust, and ultimately led to a career that was largely rebuilt outside WWE.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Penguins' Andrei Kuzmenko takes leave from team after father is killed by a bear in Russia
articles.summary: The 30-year-old signed a one-year deal to join the Penguins in July.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Penguins forward Andrei Kuzmenko is taking a leave of absence following the death of his father, Alexander.

According to Russian network REN TV , Alexander Kuzmenko was on a fishing trip with six other people in Siberia when he was attacked by a bear. He was reportedly bitten in the head and suffered severe facial injuries.

The dense forest along the Krasnaya River reportedly caused a delay in ambulances being able to reach the 62-year-old hockey coach. The group was able to get the bear away from the area before Kuzmenko was eventually airlifted to a hospital in Kyzyl where he was later pronounced dead.

Andrei Kuzmenko practiced with the Penguins on Thursday morning before departing to Russia.

"The Pittsburgh Penguins organization was deeply saddened, this morning, to learn of the passing of Andrei Kuzmenko's father, Alexander," said Pittsburgh general manager Kyle Dubas in a statement . "Our deepest thoughts and sympathies are with the Kuzmenko family and their loved ones as they grieve the loss of Alexander. We ask that the privacy of Andrei and the Kuzmenko family be respected at this time.

"Andrei chose to be surrounded by his teammates and practice with the team this morning before returning to Moscow to be with his family this afternoon. Andrei and the Kuzmenko family have the full support of the Penguins organization during this time."

Andrei Kuzmenko signed a one-year, $5 million contract to join the Penguins in the summer. After eight seasons playing in Russia's KHL, the 30-year-old signed with the Vancouver Canucks in 2022. In January 2024, he was dealt to the Calgary Flames before moving again a year later to the Philadelphia Flyers . Two months later, he was on the move again after being a trade deadline acquisition by the Los Angeles Kings , where he played through last season.

The Penguins open the 2026-27 NHL season next Wednesday night against the Flyers.

articles.title: Blackhawks sign forward Oliver Moore to a 5-year deal worth $4.25 million per year
articles.summary: The Chicago Blackhawks signed forward Oliver Moore to a five-year deal on Thursday, locking up an important piece of their long-term future.  The deal with t...
articles.body:
CHICAGO (AP) — The Chicago Blackhawks signed forward Oliver Moore to a five-year deal on Thursday, locking up an important piece of their long-term future.

The deal with the 21-year-old Moore carries an average annual value of $4.25 million.

Moore, a first-round pick by Chicago in the 2023 draft, had five goals and 14 assists in 51 games for the Blackhawks last season while averaging just under 13 minutes of ice time per game.

Moore is coming off an offseason in which he made his debut for Team USA at the world championships, picking up three assists.

articles.title: SA vs AUS 1st ODI: Marco Jansen takes stunning catch of Matt Renshaw as Dale Steyn hails compatriot
articles.summary: Dale Steyn was in awe as Marco Jansen pulled off a stunning catch to dismiss Matt Renshaw in the SA vs AUS 1st ODI at Durban. Watch the video and reactions.
articles.body:
Marco Jansen pulled off a stunning one-handed catch to dismiss Australia's Matt Renshaw, swinging the momentum firmly toward South Africa .

Fans and legend Dale Steyn flooded social media with praise, calling it one of the best catches seen in cricket this year.

South Africa completed a 67-run win, with Jansen also contributing 75 runs off 59 balls.

Dale Steyn goes wild over Marco Jansen's screamer to dismiss Matt Renshaw in Durban

South Africa star Marco Jansen produced a moment of magic against Australia that's probably going to be replayed for a while. It was a one-handed diving catch during the opening ODI at Kingsmead, Durban, that should rank among the finest seen in international cricket this year, across any format.

The catch came at a point when Australia, batting second, still had hopes of chasing the total down. On the second ball of the 37th over, Gerald Coetzee dug one in short, and Matt Renshaw, the left-handed Aussie batter, went for the pull shot.

What followed was pure theatre as Jansen sprinted in from square leg, threw himself full length, and somehow clung on with his right hand outstretched, the ball wedging between his thumb and index finger before it could touch the turf. Renshaw departed for 44 off 49 balls, having struck six boundaries, with Coetzee finishing with figures of 1 for 39 in 7.2 overs.

Fans and Dale Steyn react to Marco Jansen's viral catch

It didn't take long for the moment to blow up online, with reactions pouring in from acros the globe.

@DaleSteyn62 wrote: "Marco Jansen has the best hands in cricket".

@askfromsid (saddam) posted: "Marco Jansen is superhero from marvels ❤️".

@thesb01 (sb🤫) brought IPL into the picture and commented: "Mumbai Indians blood"

@fudgieeleven (Farhaan Behardien) added: "The best fingers 🤣"

@AdrianN99910365 (AD) shared his admiration and wrote: "Seen some great catches but wow this is up there as the best"

How Marco Jansen's catch vs Australia shaped the result in the 1st ODI in Durban

Renshaw's wicket turned out to be the crucial moment of the innings. He'd been the one recognised batter still standing, and with him gone, Australia's chase unravelled fairly quickly. At the time, the tourists were 215 for seven, needing 83 more off 82 balls.

It was a target that had looked within reach, especially with Renshaw at the crease. But suddenly it all unravelled for the Baggy Greens after Renshaw's departure.

Corbin Bosch mopped up two wickets late on, and fittingly, it was Keshav Maharaj who wrapped things up, getting Adam Zampa to slog-sweep straight to Ryan Rickelton behind the stumps, who ended the day with three catches to his name.

South Africa had earlier posted 297 for eight in their 50 overs, and Australia, in reply, could only muster 230 all out, handing the hosts a comfortable 67-run win.

Jansen's day didn't stop at that one catch, either, as he backed it up with 75 off 59 with the bat and picked up a wicket too, capping off an all-round performance in a match that'll be remembered chiefly for those few seconds of brilliance on the green.

For all the latest cricket news, opinion, and commentary, and to share your voice, head to our Facebook , Instagram, and X (Twitter) pages.

articles.title: Liverpool now 'closely following' €30m star
articles.summary: Liverpool have been linked with a whole host of players over the last couple of years. The Anfield outfit were at the centre of attention for many transfers...
articles.body:
Liverpool have been linked with a whole host of players over the last couple of years.

The Anfield outfit were at the centre of attention for many transfers during the summer and, although only four players ended up joining, they still cast their net far and wide for potential targets.

The club will also be allowed to make three changes to their Champions League squad if they wish as they chose to include Hugo Ekitike and Conor Bradley in their plans from the start .

Indeed, this did mean that Wataru Endo and Federico Chiesa were left out of the squad but, in reality, it was clear that neither of those players were going to play an important role this term.

The transfer window may have slammed shut a few weeks ago now but, that doesn't mean that the rumour mill has stopped turning with yet another player now being linked with an Anfield switch.

Liverpool are eyeing a move for Orkun Kokcu again

One of Liverpool's main problem areas this season has been their midfield.

Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have proven that they cannot play alongside one another in a double pivot and, since Alexis Mac Allister 's contract is set to expire in June 2028, the Argentinian's future is also unclear.

Of course, Trey Nyoni has burst onto the scene this season as Curtis Jones' replacement but, since he's only 19, it'll still be a while until he's able to play two 90-minute games in a week.

This has led to fans debating what their next move should be and has made them try and figure out what the best way to improve their squad is.

It's clear that Liverpool have also been thinking about this with Turkish outlet Fanatik now sharing a new midfield target that Liverpool have laid their eyes on.

"The performance of Beşiktaş's new season squad has begun to attract the attention of English clubs," they wrote .

"Premier League team Liverpool is closely following captain Orkun Kökçü. In addition, two other clubs from England are interested. It has been learned that Tottenham is monitoring young central defender Emirhan Topçu.

"Beşiktaş management is expected to adopt a cautious approach towards offers for players they added to the squad at the beginning of the season and who have become important parts of the team.

"Beşiktaş will take the technical staff's opinion into account before evaluating any offers, especially regarding Orkun Kökçü and Emirhan Topçu."

Liverpool would have to pay significantly more than the €30 million that Besiktas paid for Orkun Kokcu

As mentioned, Liverpool's midfield has been a major problem area for them.

Of all their midfielders, only Nyoni and Mac Allister can win duels which, for a double pivot, is rather worrying.

And, since Nyoni is still so young, he can hardly be relied upon each week.

So, the fact that the Reds are looking for new midfielders is hardly surprising.

Of the lot, Kokcu is probably the most out-there target for Liverpool.

He's 25 years old, spent the last couple of years in Turkiye and, when he joined Besiktas at the start of this season, they paid €30 million for him.

And, while the Turkish Super Lig is obviously not comparable to the Premier League, his performances for Besiktas will have certainly added a few extra pennies to his transfer value.

So, as out-there of a signing Kokcu would be, depending on the price tag, he could genuinely be a solid option for Liverpool.

That is, as long as they manage to clear out some of their foreign players, of course.

articles.title: Cam Schlittler is one start away from joining Ron Guidry in Yankees history
articles.summary: New York Yankees right-hander Cam Schlitter is having one of the best-ever seasons in franchise history.
articles.body:
After his electric performance in Game 3 of the American League Wild Card series versus the Boston Red Sox last season, expectations for New York Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler suddenly grew for 2026.

The 25-year-old was a seventh round selection in the 2022 draft by New York , but nonetheless rocketed through the minor leagues to make his debut in July 2025. Over that regular season, he made 14 starts with a 2.96 ERA.

With the season he had plus that exceptional showing against Boston in a winner-take-all playoff game, anyone could have said he would be a good pitcher. However, Schlittler's performance this season has somehow blown expectations out of the water.

Ahead of his 33rd and final start of the regular season Thursday versus the Tampa Bay Rays , the All-Star can make some franchise history. Per Gary Phillips of NY Daily News, Schlittler can become the third Yankee starting pitcher ever to finish a season with an ERA below 2.00.

Across 32 starts, Schlittler is 14-6 with a 1.94 ERA. He has pitched 190 ⅔ innings, striking out 234 and walking 47. He had a splendid half-season in 2025, but has impressively toned down the walks and upped the strikeouts this year.

With the way things look currently, Schlittler will win the AL Cy Young Award when it is announced in November. If so, he will become the seventh Yankee to win the award, and would join his teammate Gerrit Cole (2023) in the honor.

New York is locked into their current position of the No. 4 seed in the AL. They will host the No. 5 seed in the Wild Card round, with the winner advancing to take on the Rays in the Division Series starting Oct. 3.

In all likelihood, it will be a rematch of last year's Wild Card with the Red Sox traveling to the Bronx for a best-of-three. Including that series, Schlittler is 3-1 with a 0.56 ERA and 39 strikeouts against his hometown team in his brief career.

With the Massachusetts native taking the mound Thursday versus Tampa Bay , he likely will not pitch Game 1 against Boston next Tuesday. A normal rest schedule would have him in line for Wednesday's Game 2.
